subject: zoology
question_text: Write a short note on the pathogenicity of Entamoeba histolytica.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.44, SAQ 49). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Ulcers in the intestine
lines: The trophozoites of Entamoeba histolytica live
in the mucous and submucous layers of the large
intestine.
They secrete the enzyme histolysin, which
digests the tissue of the intestinal wall and
forms ulcers.
steps.why: Every later symptom starts at the ulcer, so the answer opens with the enzyme that makes it — the damage is chemical, not mechanical.
common_mistakes: Writing that the parasite eats the intestinal wall. It secretes histolysin, which digests the tissue.
Naming the small intestine. The ulcers form in the large intestine.
steps.memory_tip: Histolysin means tissue-dissolving, and that is what makes the ulcer.
steps.margin_note: Two lines: where it lives, then the enzyme and the ulcer.

steps.label: Amoebic dysentery
lines: The ulcers ooze blood cells, cellular debris and
bacteria into the gut.
The patient passes stools with blood and mucus,
and has bowel irregularity and abdominal pain.
This condition is called intestinal amoebiasis
or amoebic dysentery.
steps.why: The symptoms follow straight from the ulcer, so writing them in that order shows cause and effect instead of a memorised list.
common_mistakes: Calling the condition diarrhoea. Blood and mucus in the stool make it dysentery.
Leaving out the name of the condition. Both names carry the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Ulcer leaks, so the stool carries blood and mucus: that is amoebic dysentery.
steps.margin_note: What leaks, what the patient passes, then the name. Three short lines.

steps.label: Extra-intestinal amoebiasis
lines: Sometimes the trophozoites enter the blood
stream from the ulcers.
They reach the liver, the lungs, the heart, the
kidneys and the brain, and cause abscesses in
those organs.
This is called extra-intestinal or secondary
amoebiasis, and it leads to severe conditions.
steps.why: The parasite becomes dangerous only when it leaves the gut, so the route through the blood and the organs it reaches are marked separately from the dysentery.
common_mistakes: Writing that the parasite crawls to the liver. It travels in the blood stream.
Naming only the liver. Five organs are listed in the syllabus.
steps.memory_tip: Out of the gut and into the blood: liver, lungs, heart, kidneys, brain.
steps.margin_note: The route, the organs, then the name. Three lines.

steps.label: Carriers
lines: Some infected people show no symptoms at all.
Their stools still contain the tetranucleate
cysts, so they spread the infection to others.
Such people are called carriers or asymptomatic
cyst passers.
steps.why: A carrier spreads the disease while looking healthy, which is why the last mark is kept for this point rather than for another symptom.
common_mistakes: Writing that carriers are mildly ill. A carrier shows no symptoms.
Leaving out the cysts. The cyst in the stool is what makes a carrier infectious.
steps.memory_tip: No symptoms, but cysts in the stool: that is a carrier.
steps.margin_note: The term in the box, then three short lines. Closing mark.

insider_note: Pathogenicity means the damage done, so the answer must move from the ulcer to the dysentery to the spread — a description of the parasite scores nothing here.
